mechanism.base: Fire is born of wood, the old texts say, and the warmth lies hidden in the grain long before any flame shows. Dry branches feed a blaze and green ones only smoke it, so what the fire burns decides how it burns. Wood gives the flame its height and its hours, and a fire remembers every log that was laid on it, the one that caught quick and the one that would not.
mechanism.catalyst_turn: With too little Wood, the fire has nothing long to feed on, a bright start that drops to embers before the work is done. Keep one slow book going beside the fast ones.
mechanism.friction_turn: With too much Wood, the logs are stacked higher than the flame can climb, so much to take in that nothing gets lit. Finish one small thing before you read another word.

catalyst.clause: The fire has nothing long to feed on, a bright start that drops to embers.
catalyst.remedy: Keep one slow book going beside the fast ones.

friction.clause: The logs are stacked higher than the flame can climb.
friction.remedy: Finish one small thing before you read another word.

wide.clause: Wood is one thing you never run short of, the fuel laid ready for your fire.
wide.remedy: Light something with it this week.

missing.clause: No fuel under the flame, a fire lit on whatever is nearest and gone as fast.
missing.remedy: Borrow Wood from a teacher, a long book, one quiet hour.

spared.clause: No Wood to pile on, and the fire is brighter for the open air.
spared.remedy: Act on what you already know.

thin.clause: A little Wood in the fire, enough to catch and not enough to smother it.
thin.remedy: Keep it small. One book at a time.

excess.clause: Wood piled past use and the fire blazes past its task, all flare and no lasting warmth.
excess.remedy: Take in less. Put one idea to work.

function.definition_catalyst: Your Mind is where the world soaks in and becomes yours. Wood makes it grow. As a catalyst, the intake falls behind the output, and you would rather puzzle an answer out alone than take one from a teacher. Either way you run dry before you feel taught.
function.definition_friction: Your Mind is where the world soaks in and becomes yours. Here Wood makes it keep growing. As a friction, intake outruns use and you take in more than you decide on, by your odd method or the way home taught you. Your own work sits waiting while you study.
function.advise_catalyst: You give out faster than you take in, and running on your own fuel feels like energy until it runs out. Read one long book a chapter at a time. Sit with a question overnight before you answer it. Ask someone older how they did it and listen past the first sentence. Nap before the next idea.
function.advise_friction: Seek Metal, the Action energy. Metal is the finished line: it decides, it ships, it dates the thing you keep studying. Let it spend what Wood piles up. You keep learning past the point of use because being judged feels worse than being unready. Decide one open question by a written date. Hand someone one unfinished page.

candidates.cta_verdict: You learn by growing an idea rather than collecting it, so you understand late and keep it for good.

mechanism.base: Wood is warm by nature and fire sleeps inside it, the classics say, so every flame is fed by what was gathered before it: dry branches, stacked seasons, years of quiet growth surrendered to one bright hour. A fire is only ever as tall as its fuel. The blaze borrows everything from the forest.
mechanism.catalyst_turn: Run thin, the flame eats scraps: brilliance flaring on no reserves, warmth borrowed from tomorrow. Your chart asks you to stack wood. Learn, gather, befriend, store.
mechanism.friction_turn: Run heavy, the fire outgrows its hearth: every branch thrown on at once, heat spent in a rush, ash by morning. Burn one pile at a time.

catalyst.clause: The flame eats scraps: brilliance flaring on no reserves, warmth borrowed from tomorrow.

friction.clause: The fire outgrows its hearth: every branch thrown on at once, heat spent in a rush.
friction.remedy: Burn one pile at a time.

wide.clause: You were given plenty of Wood, the fuel your light was waiting for.
wide.remedy: Burn what you have gathered. Light one thing this week.

missing.clause: No fuel behind the flame: brilliance on nothing, warmth borrowed from tomorrow.

spared.clause: Wood runs absent, and the fire keeps its size: one flame, one task, burned to the end.
spared.remedy: Keep it. Gather only what you will burn.

thin.clause: Wood runs thin and unwanted: a small pile, easily burned.

excess.clause: Too much wood feeds the fire past its task: a blaze that eats a season's fuel overnight.
excess.remedy: Bank the fire. Save half the wood.

function.definition_catalyst: Wood is your Mind, and as a catalyst, it is how your fuel accumulates: skills stacked, books finished, friendships tended, people learned from over years. What you gather quietly becomes what you later spend as brilliance.
function.definition_friction: Wood is your Mind, and as a friction, it is more fuel than one flame can use: courses, books, mentors, plans, all of it feeding a fire that burns hotter than it burns long.
function.advise_catalyst: Brilliance is mostly patience with good storage. Keep one slow project that grows monthly, a course, a craft, a language, and refuse to rush it. Finish books. Choose one person to learn from properly this year and stay teachable.
function.advise_friction: You start more than you finish. Finish the one project closest to done this month, as it is, and let it ship at eighty percent. Put every new course, book or plan on a list until that one is out. When the urge to start something rises, ask which unfinished thing it would replace.

$original.cta_verdict: Your mind gathers fuel long before it flares, and the ideas you feed patiently become the insights people call sudden.
